Create a complete single self-contained file `chip8_anthropic-claude-sonnet-5_01.html` (HTML + CSS + JavaScript inline;
no external libraries, CDNs, assets or backend). Build a working CHIP-8 emulator.

Implement the interpreter properly: 4 KB of memory with the font set loaded at 0x050 and programs at 0x200,
sixteen 8-bit registers V0 to VF, the 16-bit index register, the program counter, a call stack, and the
delay and sound timers counting down at 60 Hz. Decode and execute the complete instruction set of 35
instructions, including the arithmetic and logic group with the carry and borrow flags in VF, the shift
instructions, jumps and calls, the random instruction, BCD conversion, register save and load, and the key
tests.

The display is 64 by 32 pixels drawn on a canvas scaled to a readable size, with sprites drawn by XOR and
the collision flag set in VF. The 16-key keypad is mapped to a 4 by 4 block of keyboard keys shown in the
interface; key press and release must both reach the emulator.

Include a small demo ROM as a byte array inside the file: a real program, assembled by you, that draws a
sprite and moves or reacts to a key, so that the emulator can be tried without any download. Also allow
loading a ROM from a local file.

Add run, pause, single step and reset controls, an adjustable instructions-per-frame speed, and a debugger
panel showing the registers, the index register, the program counter, the stack and the decoded current
instruction. Every visible control must work. Deliver the one file `chip8_anthropic-claude-sonnet-5_01.html`.

{"path":"chip8_anthropic-claude-sonnet-5_01.html","edit_description":"
Create a complete, self-contained CHIP-8 emulator as a single HTML file (inline CSS + JS, no externals). Requirements:

STRUCTURE: Full HTML page, dark theme styling, layout with: canvas display, control panel, keypad panel, debugger panel.

INTERPRETER (in a Chip8 class):
- memory: Uint8Array(4096)
- fontset (standard 16 chars x 5 bytes hex digits 0-F) loaded starting at 0x050
- registers V = Uint8Array(16) (V0..VF)
- I = 16-bit index register (number)
- pc = program counter, starts at 0x200
- stack = array/Uint16Array(16), sp = stack pointer
- delayTimer, soundTimer: 8-bit, decremented at 60Hz via a separate timer interval (setInterval 1000/60) independent from the main instruction-execution loop
- display: Uint8Array(64*32), 1 = pixel on
- keypad: Array(16) booleans for key states 0x0-0xF
- drawFlag for redraw
- programs loaded at 0x200
- reset()/loadRom(Uint8Array) methods that clear memory/registers/display, reload fontset, copy rom bytes into memory from 0x200
- cycle() method: fetch 2-byte opcode big-endian at pc, increment pc by 2 BEFORE executing (adjust pc for jumps/calls accordingly), decode and execute instruction, store last decoded instruction info (mnemonic string + raw opcode) for the debugger panel.

INSTRUCTION SET - implement all standard 35 CHIP-8 opcodes:
00E0 CLS, 00EE RET, 1NNN JP addr, 2NNN CALL addr, 3XKK SE Vx,byte, 4XKK SNE Vx,byte, 5XY0 SE Vx,Vy,
6XKK LD Vx,byte, 7XKK ADD Vx,byte, 8XY0 LD Vx,Vy, 8XY1 OR, 8XY2 AND, 8XY3 XOR,
8XY4 ADD Vx,Vy (VF=carry), 8XY5 SUB Vx,Vy (VF=NOT borrow), 8XY6 SHR (VF=LSB before shift),
8XY7 SUBN (VF=NOT borrow), 8XYE SHL (VF=MSB before shift), 9XY0 SNE Vx,Vy, ANNN LD I,addr,
BNNN JP V0,addr, CXKK RND Vx,byte (byte AND random 0-255), DXYN DRW Vx,Vy,nibble (XOR draw sprite from I,
width 8, height N, wrap/clip at screen edges, set VF=1 on any pixel collision), EX9E SKP Vx (key pressed),
EXA1 SKNP Vx (key not pressed), FX07 LD Vx,DT, FX0A LD Vx,K (blocking wait for a keypress — implement via a
"waiting for key" state flag that halts execution until a key event sets Vx and clears the flag),
FX15 LD DT,Vx, FX18 LD ST,Vx, FX1E ADD I,Vx, FX29 LD F,Vx (I = address of hex digit sprite for low nibble of Vx,
at 0x050 + Vx*5), FX33 LD B,Vx (BCD: store hundreds/tens/ones of Vx at I, I+1, I+2), FX55 LD [I],Vx (store V0..Vx
into memory starting at I), FX65 LD Vx,[I] (load memory starting at I into V0..Vx). Use correct quirk behavior
for classic CHIP-8 (I unchanged by FX55/FX65 is fine either way, but be consistent and document choice in a comment).

DISPLAY: <canvas> rendered at 64x32 logical pixels scaled up (e.g. 12px per pixel = 768x384 canvas), pixel-art
(imageRendering pixelated), redraw on drawFlag using 2D context fillRect, pixel-on color bright green/white on
black background.

KEYPAD: standard CHIP-8 16-key layout mapped to keyboard:
1 2 3 4        1 2 3 C
Q W E R   -->  4 5 6 D
A S D F        7 8 9 E
Z X C V        A 0 B F
Show a 4x4 grid of on-screen key buttons labeled with hex values that highlight when pressed (mouse/touch AND
keyboard). Wire both keydown/keyup window listeners (preventDefault for mapped keys) AND pointerdown/pointerup
(or mousedown/mouseup + touchstart/touchend) on the on-screen buttons, both paths must call the same
chip8.keyDown(n)/keyUp(n) methods so press and release both reach the emulator.

DEMO ROM: embed this exact byte array as the built-in demo ROM (a real assembled program: it clears screen, loads
I with the font sprite for digit 0 at 0x050, draws it at (V0=0x10,V1=0x0E), then checks key 6 (SKNP+ADD) to move
right and key 4 (SKNP+ADD) to move left each frame, then loops back to redraw):
const DEMO_ROM = new Uint8Array([
  0x60,0x10, 0x61,0x0E, 0xA0,0x50, 0x00,0xE0, 0xD0,0x15,
  0x62,0x06, 0xE2,0xA1, 0x70,0x01, 0x63,0x04, 0xE3,0xA1,
  0x70,0xFF, 0x12,0x06
]);
Load this ROM automatically on page load.

FILE LOADING: an <input type="file"> that reads the selected file as ArrayBuffer (FileReader), builds a
Uint8Array, and calls chip8.reset()+loadRom() then resumes paused state.

CONTROLS (all must be wired to working handlers):
- Run button: starts the execution loop (requestAnimationFrame driven), disabled while running
- Pause button: stops the loop, disabled while paused
- Step button: executes exactly one cycle() while paused, updates debugger
- Reset button: reloads the currently loaded ROM (demo or last-loaded file) and clears display/registers
- Speed control: a <input type="range"> (e.g. 1-200) labeled "Instructions per frame", with a live numeric
  readout, read by the run loop to call cycle() N times per animation frame (also decrement timers at 60Hz
  independently via setInterval, not tied to IPF)
- A file input to load a custom ROM

DEBUGGER PANEL (updates every frame while running, and after step/reset):
- All 16 V registers (V0-VF) shown as hex, in a grid
- I register (hex), PC (hex), delay timer, sound timer (decimal)
- The call stack (list of hex addresses, with SP)
- The current decoded instruction: raw opcode hex + human-readable mnemonic (e.g. "6A3F  LD V0, 0x10")
- Keep this panel visually distinct (monospace font, bordered box)

Make sure the whole thing is one file, no external resources, valid HTML5, and runs by opening directly in a
browser. Use clean readable vanilla JS (ES6 class), no frameworks.
"}
